facts.text: Synthetic training data are sensor data made by a simulator or generative model rather than recorded in the field; the domain gap is the difference between artificial and real data that makes a detector trained on one perform worse on the other.
facts.quote: Synthetic training data are sensor data made by a simulator or a generative model rather than recorded in the field, and the domain gap is the difference between that artificial data and real data that makes a detector trained on one do worse on the other.

facts.text: Recording a worker in every pose and at every distance in dust, snow and night is slow and sometimes dangerous.
facts.quote: Recording a worker in every pose, at every distance, in dust, snow and night is slow and sometimes dangerous.

facts.text: A simulator can render ten thousand images of workers in varied poses, distances and conditions overnight, each perfectly labeled.
facts.quote: A simulator can render ten thousand such images overnight, each perfectly labeled.

facts.text: Data augmentation stretches a small real dataset by altering real images, including flipping, darkening and adding rendered rain.
facts.quote: Data augmentation is the milder version: altering real images, flipping, darkening, adding rendered rain, to stretch a small real dataset further.

facts.text: Synthetic data can have physically unrealistic features: rendered dust scatters light differently from real dust, rendered steel returns radar differently from real steel, and rendered scenes are too clean.
facts.quote: Rendered dust does not scatter light exactly as real dust does; rendered steel does not return radar as real steel does; rendered scenes are too clean.

facts.text: A detector trained on synthetic data can learn artificial-data differences and consequently perform poorly on real data.
facts.quote: A detector trained on synthetic data learns those differences and stumbles on reality.

facts.text: Evidence across construction, mining and road studies indicates that mixing synthetic and real data generally beats real-only training in data-poor settings, while synthetic-only training leaves a domain gap.
facts.quote: mixing synthetic with real data generally beats real-only training in data-poor settings, while synthetic-only training leaves a gap [Chapter 9].

facts.text: Comparison of a simulated off-road lidar dataset with a real dataset showed large domain-shift effects.
facts.quote: A simulated off-road lidar dataset compared against a real one showed large domain-shift effects [Chapter 6]

facts.text: Image-quality scores did not reliably predict system behavior in the evidence discussed in Chapter 9.
facts.quote: image-quality scores did not reliably predict system behavior [Chapter 9].

facts.text: Training augmentation is the strongest case for generated data because the generated data need only improve generalization.
facts.quote: Using generated data for training augmentation is the strongest case, because the data need only improve generalization.

facts.text: Generated data are useful now for robustness tests of detector stability as visibility degrades, provided the test claim is explicitly about that transformation.
facts.quote: Using it for robustness tests ("does the detector stay stable as visibility degrades?") is useful now, if the claim is explicitly about that transformation.

facts.text: Using generated data as physical-equivalence evidence—for example, claiming a synthetic fog frame proves that a real camera meets a requirement at 40 m visibility—is not established and needs separate calibration against the real sensor.
facts.quote: Using it as physical-equivalence evidence ("this synthetic fog frame proves the real camera meets the requirement at 40 m visibility") is not established and needs separate calibration against the real sensor.

facts.text: Synthetic-data risks include renderer artifacts, wrong particle physics, missing contamination and vibration, and validation contamination caused by sharing a generator between training and test.
facts.quote: Risks include renderer artifacts, wrong particle physics, missing contamination and vibration, and validation contaminated by sharing a generator between training and test [Chapter 9].

facts.text: Synthetic data can widen coverage of rare and dangerous cases before the heavy-machine prototype exists.
facts.quote: Synthetic data can widen coverage of rare and dangerous cases before the prototype exists

facts.text: No study shows that synthetic-only training or validation provides field-level collision-avoidance reliability for heavy machines.
facts.quote: no study shows that synthetic-only training or validation gives field-level collision-avoidance reliability for heavy machines

facts.text: For heavy-machine collision-avoidance development and validation, synthetic data should supplement real recordings and never replace them.
facts.quote: synthetic data supplement real recordings and never replace them [Chapter 9].
